title: Vertical Stretch: y = 2f(x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the transformation taking the graph of y=f(x) to the graph of y=2f(x).

steps.title: Interpret the Multiplier
steps.explanation: Each output is doubled, so heights above the x-axis double and depths below also double in magnitude.
steps.why: Multiplication outside the function scales values vertically.

steps.title: Track a Typical Point
steps.explanation: Points move straight away from the x-axis (or toward it if nearer to it after halving) with x-coordinates fixed.
steps.why: The distance from the x-axis is multiplied by 2.

steps.title: Note the Fixed Set
steps.explanation: Where the original graph meets the x-axis, the stretched graph does too; those crossings stay put.
steps.why: Doubling zero is still zero, so intercepts on the axis anchor the transformation.

steps.title: Describe the Sketch
steps.explanation: Peaks become twice as high and valleys twice as deep, stretching the picture vertically away from the horizontal axis.
steps.why: A vertical stretch by factor 2 preserves horizontal positions entirely.
